[1/3] Plan: strict question-ref validation, validate selections before building the matrix, derive the surfaced-module inventory from the package, and correct the evidence-grouping wording; ADR-015 and gates.

impact_assessment.why: Analysis found malformed refs such as q_ and question:q_1:extra still pass the prefix-only check, invalid selections pay for a full matrix build before failing, the inventory module list is hardcoded, and the docstring says grouped by link kind although non-role kinds land in other.
impact_assessment.benefits: Malformed selections fail before any work, the self-checking inventory covers future modules and assignment forms automatically, and the evidence contract is described as implemented.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: get_evidence_matrix validates before building and rejects more malformed values; dependency: stdlib only; concurrency: none; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Add failing-first tests for the malformed refs and build-order guard, then tighten _question_key, move validation before build, harden the inventory helper, record ADR-015, update README, refresh the map and run the gates.

[1/4] Failing-first tests for a turnkey LatticeClient: connection lifecycle, MCP-parity call_tool over all 21 tools, tool schemas, convenience methods, closed-client errors, and an async facade on a dedicated thread. [2/4] Publish dispatch_tool in lattice.mcp and add lattice/client.py with LatticeClient/AsyncLatticeClient. [3/4] Export the client from lattice.api, record ADR-016, update README and the codebase map. [4/4] Run every Phase 4 gate, record checklists and complete.

impact_assessment.why: lattice.api is a stable library surface but not a turnkey AI integration: callers must manage the SQLite connection, map MCP schemas to calls themselves, and async agent hosts have no safe wrapper. The neurocore draft expects an async adapter that does not exist.
impact_assessment.benefits: An AI host imports one client, enters a context manager, lists 21 JSON tool schemas and calls any tool by name with identical behavior to the MCP server; a dedicated-thread async facade makes the same surface safe for asyncio hosts without changing sqlite thread settings.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: mcp._dispatch becomes public dispatch_tool and api gains two client classes plus DEFAULT_DB; dependency: standard library copy/concurrent.futures/asyncio only; concurrency: the async facade serializes all work on one dedicated thread; state: the client owns one existing connection and closes it; no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Build the sync client as a thin wrapper over the existing MCP dispatch so tool semantics cannot drift, prove parity against TOOLS in tests, run async calls on one executor thread so SQLite keeps its thread affinity, and close idempotently in the context manager.

Published mcp.dispatch_tool, exported the client from lattice.api, recorded ADR-016, updated README and the map. checklists: passed; 159/159 tests; aikit check lattice 4/4 gates. Task 'lattice-client-adapter-v1' completed successfully.

[1/4] Failing-first tests: read-only mode filters schemas and blocks every write/IO tool, db_path rejects empty/None, resource/prompt metadata and reads exist, and all 21 tools execute with JSON-serializable payloads. [2/4] Implement read_only, path validation, public read_resource/get_prompt, and client resource/prompt helpers. [3/4] Record ADR-017, update README and the codebase map. [4/4] Run every Phase 4 gate and complete.

impact_assessment.why: The analysis found the new client has no read-only/sandboxed mode: an autonomous agent gets every write tool, arbitrary snapshot paths and network discovery. It also accepts an empty or None database path, hides resources/prompts, and only spot-checks tool execution.
impact_assessment.benefits: A host can hand an agent a read-only client whose schema list contains only safe tools, while resources and prompts gain the same first-class client parity as tools; every tool's payload is frozen by a table-driven test.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: LatticeClient gains read_only and repository becomes unavailable in that mode; MCP gains public read_resource/get_prompt functions; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: unchanged single-thread serialization; state: no schema change.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Enforce read-only both in tool_schemas and call_tool, reject auto_link writes, keep the raw repository unavailable in read-only mode, validate the path before opening, refactor MCP resource/prompt helpers into public functions, and pin each tool through the client.

checkpoints.description: [2/4]-[4/4] Delivered read-only LatticeClient policy: 12-tool schema filter with auto_link removed, call_tool rejects writes/network/snapshot tools and auto_link, repository hidden; db_path validation; public mcp.read_resource/get_prompt plus client resource/prompt schemas and readers; ADR-017, README and map updated. checklists: passed; 164/164 tests; aikit check lattice 4/4 gates. Task 'lattice-client-safety-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Hybrid tests: read-only open must not create a missing file, must enforce query_only, must refuse a v1 migration, must work for :memory:; client read-only must require an existing DB; malformed prompt tokens/arguments must return -32602. [2/3] Add open_database(read_only), close-on-failure, SQLite mode=ro/query_only and schema verification; harden get_prompt arguments. [3/3] Update ADR-017, README, map and run gates.

impact_assessment.why: Verification showed a read-only client still created/migrated the database and the MCP prompt endpoint leaked ValueError instead of a JSON-RPC error; the async repository error also disagreed with the sync client.
impact_assessment.benefits: Read-only is now a file-level guarantee as well as a tool-surface policy, malformed prompts fail safely at the protocol boundary, and both client facades raise the same LatticeError for repository access.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: open_database gains a backward-compatible read_only keyword and refuses missing/v1 files in that mode; dependency: standard library sqlite3/pathlib only; concurrency: unchanged; state: read-only paths do not write or migrate.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Open existing read-only files with mode=ro and query_only, verify the schema without migrating, close connections on every failure path, validate prompt arguments before synthesis, and pin each behavior with database, client and MCP tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/3]-[3/3] Delivered file-level read-only opens: open_database(path, read_only=True) requires an existing file, uses SQLite mode=ro plus query_only, verifies the schema without migrating, and closes on failure. LatticeClient read-only requires an existing DB; get_prompt validates token/argument types so MCP returns -32602; async repository now raises LatticeError. ADR-017, README and map updated. checklists: passed; 170/170 tests; aikit check lattice 4/4 gates. Uncommitted by PRINCIPLE-018 R1.
Task 'lattice-readonly-db-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Failing-first tests for truthy non-object MCP params and arguments, direct dispatch_tool with non-dict arguments, and open_database(None/empty). [2/3] Preserve params instead of masking falsy values, validate mapping shapes in both handlers and dispatch_tool, and type/empty-check the database path. [3/3] Record the WAL and allowlist caveats in ADR-017/README, refresh the map and run gates.

impact_assessment.why: Verification showed remaining crashes: resources/read and prompts/get raised AttributeError for truthy list params, and open_database(None) raised TypeError instead of the LatticeError contract; direct dispatch_tool had the same unvalidated-shape gap.
impact_assessment.benefits: Every malformed JSON-RPC params/arguments shape now returns -32602, direct Python callers get the Error/Why/Fix triad from dispatch_tool and open_database, and the read-only WAL/allowlist limitations are documented.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: MCP rejects empty-list params that previously fell through to unknown-resource errors, and open_database rejects None/empty paths; dependency: standard library os.PathLike only; concurrency: unchanged; state: none.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Keep the original params object, guard each handler and dispatcher with an isinstance dict check, validate path types and emptiness before Path/sqlite work, and pin every boundary with MCP and database tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/3]-[3/3] Delivered MCP boundary validation: params are preserved (empty list no longer becomes {}), resources/read and prompts/get reject non-object params with -32602, tools/call rejects non-object arguments, and public dispatch_tool raises LatticeError for non-dict arguments. open_database validates path type and emptiness before Path/sqlite. ADR-017/README document WAL and allowlist caveats. checklists: passed; 173/173 tests; aikit check lattice 4/4 gates. Uncommitted by PRINCIPLE-018 R1.
Task 'lattice-protocol-params-v1' completed successfully.

[1/3] Failing-first tests: client.call_tool and dispatch_tool reject non-string tool names, and LatticeClient/open_database normalize a whitespace-wrapped :memory: sentinel while preserving real paths. [2/3] Add name guards and align client/database path normalization. [3/3] Refresh the map, run gates and complete.

impact_assessment.why: Verification found two low API inconsistencies: an unhashable tool name crashes only the read-only allowlist check, and LatticeClient strips path whitespace while open_database preserves it.
impact_assessment.benefits: Both entry points reject malformed names with the Error/Why/Fix triad, and a database path opens the same way through the client and the database layer, including a whitespace-wrapped :memory: sentinel.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: non-string tool names now fail consistently; dependency: none; concurrency: none; state: path handling changes only for whitespace around the sentinel and for previously stripped real paths.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Validate names before any set membership or dispatch, normalize only the :memory: sentinel in one shared style, preserve other path text, and pin both behaviors with client, MCP and database tests.

checkpoints.description: [2/3]-[3/3] Added string-name guards to LatticeClient.call_tool and public dispatch_tool, made tools/call reject blank names with -32602, and normalized a whitespace-wrapped :memory: sentinel in both LatticeClient and open_database while preserving real path text. checklists: passed; 177/177 tests; aikit check lattice 4/4 gates.
